title: Shield Forge Agents Automate Legacy Portal Work With OpenAI
summary: Shield deploys OpenAI-powered Forge agents to handle repetitive legacy portal tasks, freeing IT technicians to focus on complex judgment calls.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- Shield's Forge agents use OpenAI to navigate legacy portals and execute routine IT tasks without human intervention.
- IT technicians hand off repetitive portal work to agents, focusing instead on issues requiring technical judgment.
- Officially launched on November 13, 2026, targeting enterprises with outdated systems and overwhelmed support teams.


Shield has officially released Forge agents, an OpenAI-powered automation layer designed to handle repetitive tasks inside legacy IT portals. Officially launched on November 13, 2026, the solution targets enterprises struggling with outdated ticketing systems and overwhelmed IT support teams. Forge agents navigate aging interfaces, execute routine workflows, and log actions so technicians can focus on problems requiring human judgment.


## How Forge Agents Interact With Legacy Portals


Forge agents connect to existing IT service management platforms through APIs and browser automation. When a technician assigns a ticket category tagged for automation, the agent reads the request, navigates the necessary[legacy modernization](https://emergent.sh/glossary/legacy-modernization) portal screens, fills forms, and completes the workflow. The agent documents every step in the ticket log, maintaining an audit trail identical to manual entries.


According to Shield's case studies, common automated tasks include password resets, software license provisioning, and access permission updates. The system does not replace the portal itself but acts as a persistent operator layer on top of it.


## Release Date and Availability


Shield introduced Forge agents to enterprise customers on November 13, 2026. The product is currently available to organizations with existing Shield contracts and can be deployed within legacy environments that meet minimum API access requirements. Pricing follows a per-agent-per-month model, with discounts for volume deployments across multiple service desks.


## OpenAI Integration and Technical Architecture


Forge agents rely on[OpenAI](https://emergent.sh/learn/what-is-openai) models to parse natural language ticket descriptions, infer required portal actions, and adapt to interface variations across different legacy systems. The agents use OpenAI's reasoning capabilities to handle edge cases, such as incomplete ticket details or ambiguous user requests, by querying the technician before proceeding.


Shield has not disclosed which specific OpenAI model powers Forge, but technical documentation references GPT-4-class reasoning for decision trees and form field mapping. The agents operate within isolated environments to prevent cross-tenant data exposure.


## Benefits for IT Technicians and Service Teams


Shield reports that pilot customers reduced average ticket resolution time by 40 percent for automatable tasks. Technicians no longer spend hours cycling through portal screens for routine requests, instead triaging only issues that require troubleshooting or escalation. The system also reduces after-hours workload by processing queued tickets overnight without human supervision.


- Eliminates manual portal navigation for repetitive requests
- Maintains compliance audit trails automatically
- Scales across multiple legacy systems without retraining staff
- Frees technicians to focus on complex technical problems


## What This Means for Enterprise IT


Shield's Forge agents represent a practical application of AI in environments where full system replacement is not feasible. Many enterprises operate critical business functions on decades-old portals that lack modern APIs or user interfaces. By layering intelligent automation on top of these systems, organizations can extend their lifespan while improving service desk efficiency. The launch signals growing demand for AI solutions that work with existing infrastructure rather than requiring costly migrations.
